title: The Lark and Her Young Ones
summary: A lark nested in a ripe wheat field. Hearing the farmer say he would ask his neighbors to help reap, the wise mother told her chicks not to worry....
full_text:
Along a dusty rural road that wound between stone walls and sun-drenched vineyards, A lark nested in a ripe wheat field. Hearing the farmer say he would ask his neighbors to help reap, the wise mother told her chicks not to worry..... The creatures of the field went about their daily lives according to their nature, each seeking their own advantage while keeping a vigilant watch over friends and foes alike.

As the hours passed, an unexpected turning point arose that tested their wits and character. A tense confrontation soon arose as rival desires crossed paths under the midday sun. Words were exchanged with cautious cunning, glances were measured, and each party sought to disguise their true intentions behind a veil of outward innocence.

Yet the timeless laws of nature cannot be deceived by clever words or false appearances. Natural instincts and sharp wits collided, bringing the trial to an immediate, decisive climax.  The outcome was swift and irreversible, leaving behind a lasting lesson for all who witnessed the event, proving that if you want a thing done, do it yourself; do not depend upon neighbors or kin.
moral: If you want a thing done, do it yourself; do not depend upon neighbors or kin.
